Plot and report the interactions from a Bayesian mixed model

Source: R/bayes_mm_interact.R
bayes_mm_interact.Rd

For each interaction you ask for, prints a table of the estimated means and contrasts, and draws a plot of the estimated means with their posterior distributions. Works for interactions between factors, and for interactions between one continuous variable and one or two factors. Any arguments of eyethinkdata::pirateye() can be passed in to change the plot.

Usage

bayes_mm_interact(
  bmm,
  interacts = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  pred_values = NULL,
  ribbon = T,
  ladder = F,
  spark = F,
  slope_mpes = T,
  mfx_sideplot = F,
  ylim = NULL,
  contrast_sparkline = F,
  show_mpe = T,
  show_preddist = T,
  ...
)

Arguments

bmm

A model from bayes_mm_run() (or the list returned by bayes_mm()).

interacts

The interactions to plot, as a vector of text with the conditions separated by ":", eg c("adcon:tv", "adcon:age:tv"). If missing, all of the interactions in the model are plotted. Remember that punctuation is replaced by underscores in the names of conditions.

title

Extra text for the title of the plot (and the file name).

pred_values

For continuous variables, a vector of values at which to make predictions. Default is 10 equally spaced values.

ribbon

For continuous variables, shade the region where there is no evidence that the lines differ?

ladder

For continuous variables, write the MPE for the difference between lines at each predicted value?

spark

For continuous variables, plot the MPEs at each predicted value in a panel below?

slope_mpes

For continuous variables, write the MPE for each slope on the plot?

mfx_sideplot

For continuous variables with a two level first factor, add a small plot on the left of the posterior distributions of the main effect of that factor.

ylim

Limits for the y axis, as a vector of two numbers.

contrast_sparkline

For factors, show the distribution of the contrast estimates below the plot?

show_mpe

For factors, write the MPEs on the plot?

show_preddist

For factors, show the posterior distributions of the means?

...

Further arguments for eyethinkdata::pirateye(), eg bars = TRUE, violin = FALSE, and outp to change where the pdf is saved (outp = "" to not save it).

Value

A named list of plots, one for each interaction (named like "adcon:tv").

Details

The order of the conditions in an interaction matters. The first is used for the colour split, the second for the x axis, and the third, if there is one, splits the plot into panels. The MPEs shown on the plot (the probability that there is a difference) are for the effect of the first condition at each level of the others.

Factors only. The estimated means are shown with the distributions of the estimates as split violins, and with the MPE for the difference between the colour conditions at each x position.

One continuous variable. Predictions are plotted as lines at pred_values points along the x axis (by default 10 equally spaced points), and the MPE that the slope of each line is not zero is shown. If the first factor has two levels, the area where there is no evidence that the lines differ (MPE below 90%) is shaded grey (ribbon), the MPE for the difference at each point can be written on the plot (ladder), or plotted below (spark). Only one continuous variable is allowed in an interaction; if there are two, the function stops and returns a message.

See also

bayes_mm(), bayes_mm_mainFX(), eyethinkdata::pirateye()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bayes_mm_interact(bmm, interacts = "adcon:tv", bars = TRUE, violin = FALSE)
# a continuous variable (age), split by two levels of adcon and tv
bayes_mm_interact(bmm, interacts = "adcon:age:tv", ladder = TRUE, ribbon = FALSE)
} # }
